title: Singular personal pronouns
summary: Learn the three subject pronouns for one person.
objectives: Match minä, sinä, and hän to their meanings.
Distinguish speaker, addressee, and another person.
Use hän without adding gender information.

sections.title: Three roles in a sentence
paragraphs: A personal pronoun is a short word that points to a person. Minä means “I”, the speaker. Sinä means “you”, one person being addressed.
Hän refers to one other person. Finnish hän does not tell you whether that person is male or female.

sections.title: Forms first
paragraphs: This pack practises the forms used in careful writing. Learn the full pronouns before you begin matching them with verbs.
The dots over ä are part of the letter. Write minä, sinä, and hän with ä.
keyPoints: Keep ä in all three forms
Do not guess gender from hän

steps: Choose the first-person singular pronoun minä.
Choose the second-person singular pronoun sinä.
Choose hän; the pronoun itself does not mark gender.

commonMistakes: Do not remove the dots from ä.
Do not use hän for the person who is speaking.
Do not add a gender distinction that Finnish hän does not express.
